title: Saint Alphonsus Liguori, Bishop and Doctor of the Church
short_summary: Saint Alphonsus Liguori was an Italian bishop, founder of the Redemptorists, and Doctor of the Church whose moral theology shaped Catholic pastoral practice for generations.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps his memorial on August 1.
He was born near Naples in 1696 and trained first as a lawyer.
He founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, known as the Redemptorists, in 1732.
Pope Pius IX declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1871.

sections.heading: From law to the priesthood
sections.body: Alphonsus Liguori practiced law in Naples before turning to the priesthood after a professional setback led him to reconsider his path. He was ordained in 1726 and devoted himself to preaching missions among the poor and neglected in the countryside around Naples.

sections.heading: Founder of the Redemptorists
sections.body: In 1732 Alphonsus founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer to continue mission preaching among the rural poor. The Redemptorists spread beyond Italy and remain committed to evangelization among those least served by the Church.

sections.heading: Moral theologian and Doctor of the Church
sections.body: Alphonsus wrote extensively on moral theology, seeking a middle path between excessive rigor and excessive laxity in the confessional. His writings shaped Catholic pastoral practice for generations, and Pope Pius IX named him a Doctor of the Church in 1871.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Mercy in the confessional
catholic_connection_sections.body: Alphonsus's moral theology sought to guide confessors toward genuine mercy grounded in truth, neither excusing sin nor overwhelming the penitent with excessive severity.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Mission to the neglected
catholic_connection_sections.body: His preaching to the rural poor reflects the Church's ongoing call to bring the Gospel to those furthest from ordinary pastoral care.
